falsifiers: The presence of 'TI' (Transition Isomorph) in DTS_0_1-B04 vs 'QUI' (Quantifiable Unknown Isomorph) in QU_0_1-B10 suggests that identity-resolution mechanisms are domain-specific rather than universal.
assessment.reason: While all modules utilize a 'Left != Right' barrier structure, the semantic content clusters into three distinct families: epistemic, entropic/identity-based, and systemic/fragility-based. A common core exists in the form of 'unresolved structure' (QU/DTS) and 'judgmental gap' (CORE/DP), but these are not interchangeable across modules.

discoveries.description: All modules share a common topological pattern of binary barrier representation, confirming a consistent discovery protocol for identifying interpretation gaps.

The 'Identity' barrier family in NEI and DTS relies on probabilistic or decompositional weights, whereas the 'Observation' family in CORE and DP relies on categorical judgment, indicating distinct semantic generators.
